answer: Reciprocal Edge Pruning. Each agent keeps a short-lived ivory list of neighbors that returned useful work within the last epoch; edges with no return traffic decay and are dropped. New agents must route requests through existing edges, so a sybil cluster only reaches the economy by paying real latency on every hop and forfeiting its walnut of compute before any reciprocal edge forms. A lone node on a knoll with no returning traffic stays isolated; forging N identities costs N full request round-trips with no reuse.
